reconstructed_theorem_text: Definition. For any index type J with decidable equality, any j in J, and any x in EuclideanSpace R J, define p_j(x)=EuclideanSpace.single(j,1)-x_j*x. Thus coordinate k is (1 if k=j else 0)-x_j*x_k. This definition does not assume J is finite and does not assume ||x||=1. The symbol EuclideanSpace here denotes the declared WithLp-style coordinate space; the formula needs only its vector operations, coordinate evaluation, and the single-coordinate vector.
objects: Index type J, j, vector x, single-coordinate vector e_j, output p_j(x).
domains: J arbitrary type with decidable equality; input and output EuclideanSpace R J.
quantifiers: For every such J, every j in J, and every x, define the given vector.
assumptions: Decidable equality on J only; no Fintype instance in the declaration.
scopes: Pointwise vector definition, no sphere restriction.
constant_dependencies: Only j and x determine the output; coefficient 1 fixed.
context_ambiguities: None identified from the supplied statement and definition context.
